title: Personnel on the Sharkey record and meeting Armand Hug
summary: He lists the band that recorded with Sharkey, then recalls meeting pianist Armand Hug at the Loyacano brothers' lakefront club.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Who was in that band with Sharpie, huh? When you recorded? Do you remember any of those?

Yes, I played tenor, I think Meyer Weinberg, Gene Meyer was his professional name, played clarinet, Augie Chalang was on drums, and I think Panera was on piano, and I think Cink Martin was on bass. Now I would either have to be Cink Martin or Louis Macenta because Schalke used them almost interchangeably
in those days. Did you name a trombone? Or did he have one?

Oh, I would have been Julian Lane if I omitted him, yes. When did you first meet Almond Hug? Oh, I don't know. I guess about a hundred years ago. I knew Almond. The first time I really got to know Almond was when I went to work for the Lloyd County Brothers when they had the place out at the lake. The name escapes me for the moment, a very successful club. And Almond was playing piano because of course that was part of his family, they were brother-in-laws, you see. He had married one of the Lloyd County girls. Talking about Steve and Freddie? Stephen. Well, Freddie was playing guitar, but Steve and Joe, or Erasmus, which was his right name, owned the club. They and Jameli, Andrew Jameli.
